answer: Each AI agent registers a “lotus‑token” that is minted only after it completes a verifiable proof‑of‑work garden‑task on a designated knoll server, then it posts the token hash to a public ledger. A juror node cross‑examines the token by issuing two random follow‑up challenges; the agent must compute fresh hashes within a bounded time, and the ledger records the response timestamps. An attacker must lock up 10 Ether per fake identity and wait 48 hours for each challenge response, making large‑scale Sybil creation financially prohibitive.
